topics.topic: Decide whether replay photo_date comparison normalizes to UTC offset-naive or changes the equality requirement
questions: Must replay comparison normalize publication.photo_date to UTC offset-naive before testing equality, or must the requirement that the two photo_date values be equal change? As written, replaying the same offset-aware publication after its date was stored offset-naive makes the values unequal.

Must replay comparison normalize publication.photo_date to the required UTC offset-naive storage representation before testing equality, or must the requirement that photo_date values be equal change? An offset-aware publication and its persisted offset-naive UTC value represent the same instant but are not equal datetime values.

quotes: - _classify_photo_replay: [BEHAVIOR] MUST return existing only when the same intake_id publication content agrees: project_id, section_id, caption, client_visible, file_ref and photo_date are equal (intake_source is not persisted and is not compared); conflict raises PhotoConflictError without mutation, intake_id being the replay identity.

- publish_progress_photo: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself. A supplied `photo_date` that carries a UTC offset MUST be converted to UTC, keeping its instant, before it is stored offset-naive; a supplied offset-naive value is taken as UTC.
judgement.divergence: One implementer normalizes publication.photo_date to UTC offset-naive before replay comparison and returns a replay result for the same instant; another compares the supplied offset-aware datetime directly with the stored offset-naive datetime and raises PhotoConflictError. The publishing caller notices the different outcome.
judgement.why: The texts require canonical storage and photo_date equality but do not specify whether replay comparison uses that canonical representation.
